name: Pitjantjatjara

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Pitjantjatjara (pitj1243).

notes: Pama-Nyungan (Wati) language of Central Australia, with a well-established standard orthography. Retroflex consonants are written with an underline (ṯ ṉ ḻ ṟ); the common ASCII substitutions rt/rn/rl are also mapped to the same retroflex values. The palatal series is tj/ny/ly, ng is the velar nasal, single r is an alveolar trill/tap and ṟ the retroflex approximant. Long vowels are written by doubling (aa ii uu). Word-initial stress and the intervocalic voicing of stops (unmarked in spelling) are left unencoded. VOWELS: the three-vowel system a/i/u surfaces as the lowered/centralised allophones [ɐ]/[ɪ]/[ʊ] (long aa/ii/uu likewise [ɐː]/[ɪː]/[ʊː]), not the cardinal [a]/[i]/[u] the letters suggest -- attested throughout the WikiPron pjt_latn_narrow gold (e.g. alu [ɐlʊ], ini [ɪnɪ], kuka [kʊkɐ]) and consistent with Western Desert language descriptions of the Wati subgroup (e.g. Goddard, C. (1985), A Grammar of Yankunytjatjara, IAD Press, on the same three-vowel Wati system).
